Genome-wide association scan with the assembled covariances

Source: R/gwas.R
indri_gwas.Rd

Tests each SNP for association with the traits in Y, either jointly (one multi-trait "any effect" test per SNP) or trait by trait, in a linear mixed model with relationship matrix A or in a linear model. The multi-trait mixed model uses the genetic and residual covariances G and E, usually from fit_G(), which is what makes it feasible for many traits.

Usage

indri_gwas(
  Y,
  genotypes,
  fit = NULL,
  G = NULL,
  E = NULL,
  A = NULL,
  X = NULL,
  snp_info = NULL,
  mode = c("multi_trait", "single_trait"),
  model = c("lmm", "lm"),
  single_trait_variance = c("reml", "fit"),
  delta = NULL,
  dominance = FALSE,
  gxe = NULL,
  adjust = c("none", "bonferroni", "effective"),
  n_permutations = 0L,
  fdr = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  cores = 1L,
  chunk_size = 1000L
)

Arguments

Y

Numeric matrix, individuals by traits, with no missing values.

genotypes

Numeric matrix, individuals by SNPs (typically 0/1/2). Missing values are replaced by the SNP's mean; monomorphic SNPs get NA.

fit

An indri_fit from fit_G() supplying G and E, or an indri_fit_env from fit_G_env() for an environment-specific background; see that section.

G, E

Genetic and residual covariance matrices of the traits, in the units of Y, instead of fit. Matched to the columns of Y by name when both are named. For the multi-trait LM, E replaces the residual covariance.

A

Relationship matrix of the individuals; required for model = "lmm".

X

Fixed-effects design with full column rank that can represent a constant, as for fit_G(); defaults to an intercept. Principal components go here.

snp_info

Optional data frame with one row per column of genotypes (for example snp, chrom, pos), carried into the results.

mode

"multi_trait" for one joint test per SNP, "single_trait" for one test per SNP and trait.

model

"lmm" (with A) or "lm".

single_trait_variance

For the single-trait LMM, "reml" fits each trait's variance ratio, "fit" takes it from G and E.

delta

Optional fixed variance ratio for the LMMs, instead of the fitted one: a number for the multi-trait test, one value per trait for the single-trait test.

dominance

If TRUE, also fit a dominance (heterozygote) effect for each SNP; see the Dominance section. Needs genotypes coded 0, 1 and 2.

gxe

Names of columns of X (environments, such as sex, diet or a covariate) whose interaction with each SNP's additive effect is also fitted; see the Genotype-by-environment section. A factor enters as the indicator columns X has for it.

adjust

Single-trait p-value adjustment for the number of traits: "bonferroni" multiplies by P, "effective" by indri_effective_tests() of the residuals after X; both cap at 1.

n_permutations

Number of genotype permutations for empirical p-values (0, the default, for none); see the Permutations section.

fdr

Optional false discovery rate for a p-value threshold estimated from the permutations; without n_permutations it runs 10 permutations (LiMMBo's number).

seed

Optional seed for the permutations; the caller's random stream is restored afterwards.

cores

Number of processes for the permuted scans (forked; one on Windows).

chunk_size

Number of SNPs rotated at a time.

Value

An object of class indri_gwas: pvalues (a vector over SNPs, or SNPs by traits), a (the additive effects, SNPs by traits, in the units of Y per allele; not to be confused with the relationship matrix A), delta, pvalues_adjust and n_tests when adjusted, snp_info, mode, model and call. With dominance = TRUE also pvalues_dominance, d (the dominance effects: the heterozygote's deviation from the homozygotes' midpoint) and dominance_estimable; pvalues_adjust then adjusts the joint test. With gxe, also pvalues_gxe, gxe (SNPs by traits by environments), gxe_estimable and gxe_terms; pvalues_adjust then adjusts the joint test. With permutations, pvalues_empirical, qvalues_empirical and n_permutations, and with fdr, fdr and fdr_threshold.

Models

For N individuals, P traits and one SNP g, Y = X B + g beta' + U + Eps. Every test profiles an overall scale sigma^2 and is a likelihood-ratio test:

  • multi-trait LMM: vec(U + Eps) ~ N(0, sigma^2 (G (x) A + delta E (x) I)), P degrees of freedom. G and E set the shape; the ratio delta is fitted once by REML under the null (no SNP) and held fixed for every SNP. With G and E fitted to the same data it should be near 1, and is returned so that it can be checked.

  • multi-trait LM: sigma^2 E (x) I, P degrees of freedom, with E by default the covariance of the residuals of Y on X.

  • single-trait LMM: per trait, sigma^2 (A + delta I), one degree of freedom, with delta fitted by REML under the null (single_trait_variance = "reml") or taken as E[k, k] / G[k, k] ("fit").

  • single-trait LM: ordinary least squares.

Dominance

With dominance = TRUE each SNP enters as its additive dosage (0/1/2) and a heterozygote indicator (1 for genotype 1, 0 for both homozygotes). pvalues is then the joint test of both terms (2 degrees of freedom per trait), pvalues_dominance the test of the dominance term with the additive one in the null (1 per trait), and a and d the additive and dominance effects of the joint model. A SNP observed in only two genotype classes has a dominance term collinear with its dosage: it keeps the additive-only test in pvalues, gets NA dominance results, and is FALSE in dominance_estimable. Missing genotypes are imputed by the column mean in each coding. The variance ratio is fitted without any SNP, as without dominance.

Genotype-by-environment

With gxe, each SNP's dosage g also enters multiplied by each named column e of X (g * e), next to the environments' main effects, which are in X already. pvalues is then the joint test of the SNP's main effect and its interactions (and dominance), with P * (1 + n_gxe [+ 1]) degrees of freedom for P traits, and pvalues_gxe tests the interactions with the main effect (and dominance) in the null. a is the main effect (the SNP's effect where every named environment is 0) and gxe holds the interaction effects (SNPs by traits by environments). With dominance = TRUE the dominance term is a main effect only and pvalues_dominance tests it given the rest. A SNP whose interactions cannot be estimated (for instance every carrier in one environment) keeps the test without them, gets NA interaction results, and is FALSE in gxe_estimable. The covariance is the same as without gxe: GxE in the background (a polygenic G x E, or a residual variance that differs between environments) is not modelled.

Environment-specific background

With fit from fit_G_env(), the polygenic background has its own genetic covariance in each group of a discrete environment and between groups, and its own residual covariance in each: the covariance of the traits of individuals i and j is A_ij G[(env_i), (env_j)] plus, for i = j, delta E[(env_i)]. This is the background to use with gxe on that environment: unmodelled polygenic GxE inflates the interaction tests. The covariance is no Kronecker product, so the scan rotates by a generalized eigendecomposition of its genetic and residual parts, once per connected component of A: fast for families (a block-diagonal A), cubic in the number of individuals times traits for a dense A. delta is fitted by REML as usual; single_trait_variance does not apply.

Permutations

With n_permutations > 0 the genotype rows are permuted across individuals and the scan rerun, keeping the null variance ratio of the observed scan. pvalues_empirical is then (1 + #{permuted p <= observed p}) / (n_permutations + 1), per SNP (and trait); with dominance = TRUE it refers to the joint test.

The permuted scans also estimate the false discovery rate, per SNP (for single-trait scans, from each SNP's smallest adjusted p-value, or raw without adjust): at a threshold t, FDR(t) = (mean # permuted p <= t per permutation) / (# observed p <= t). qvalues_empirical is, for each SNP, the smallest FDR(t) over thresholds at or above its own p-value, and with fdr, fdr_threshold is the largest observed p-value with FDR(t) <= fdr (NA if none): the SNPs at or below it are the discoveries at that rate. (LiMMBo's "empirical FDR" was the fdr-quantile of the permuted p-values, which is close to fdr itself and so an uncorrected threshold.) Permutations are drawn in the main process (set.seed(seed), then n_permutations calls to sample.int(N)), so results do not depend on cores.

Relatedness. Permuting genotypes across individuals treats them as exchangeable, which related individuals are not: the permuted null breaks the link between genotype and relatedness that the mixed model accounts for. The empirical p-values follow LiMMBo and are a check on the analytic ones, not a replacement for them in structured samples.

The covariance is diagonalised once (eigenvectors of A, then of G relative to E), so the scan costs one N x N rotation of the genotypes plus O(N P) per SNP.

References

Meyer, H. V., Casale, F. P., Stegle, O., and Birney, E. (2018). LiMMBo: a simple, scalable approach for linear mixed models in high-dimensional genetic association studies. bioRxiv, preprint. doi:10.1101/255497
